candidates.question_text: Describe how people who use or are affected by your AI-enabled processes (staff operating the tools, and customers or other end users where relevant) report errors, harmful outputs or problems. How do you check that this reporting route actually works, and what do you review to judge it (for example submission volumes, time to acknowledge, share of reports resolved)?

How are appeals or challenges against an AI-assisted outcome (for example a decision, recommendation or response a person disputes) recorded and categorised, and who analyses the type, rate and results of those appeals? Where can the last review of this analysis be seen?

How do you measure whether intended users and affected people know the feedback channel exists and actually use it? Describe the participation or awareness measures you track, how often you review them, and what you did the last time they were low.

Give an example of feedback or appeal data changing how your organisation evaluates or tests an AI system's performance or impact (for example a new metric, test case or review threshold). Who decided on the change, and where is the decision recorded?

When end user or community feedback about an AI use is analysed, which domain experts (for example the business process owner, legal, or a subject-matter specialist) take part, how often does this happen, and what record shows their input and the resulting actions?
